correctness.rationale: An edge-wise Kirchhoff calculation gives \(\Sigma=-(I+i\sin(k\ell)G)(I-i\sin(k\ell)G)^{-1}\) where G is a port principal resolvent. The inverse Cayley transform is valid for all nonexceptional k and is injective. Both SRGs satisfy \(A^2=4I+2J\) and \(AJ=6J\), whence the exact resolvent identifies port subgraph adjacency with Σ. Both graphs realize all four triple types, whereas the rook has \(K_4\) and Shrikhande has no \(K_4\) because neighborhoods are \(C_6\). The exact rational verifier reconstructs these identities, all ≤4 induced patterns, and the \(k\ell=\pi/3\) witness. The excluded energies are not claimed.

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is the sharp minimum number of scattering terminals separating the attainable-response sets of the specific 16-vertex cospectral pair, not the general Cayley/M-function formula or the classical clique distinction. Primary full texts for the 2022 and 2023 papers and the 2025 M-function paper were compared. The former treats one lead and other graph families, the 2023 text gives general scattering Green functions, and the 2025 article presents germ constructions, none of which asserts the four-terminal minimum for this pair. Published published-finding corpus searches showed closest different graphs/invariants. A differently indexed equivalent multi-port classification remains possible.

value.rationale: A sharp measurement-channel resource threshold on the canonical smallest nonisomorphic SRG pair is an inverse-scattering problem rather than an ad hoc small matrix count. The exact three-port impossibility for every placement and the constructive four-port witness at an explicit single frequency are both meaningful. The result explains concretely why bulk cospectrality and local scattering with \(\le3\) probes fail, while four contacts suffice, without claiming general graph reconstruction.
